On the 58 admitted tuples, a final root changes in 38 tuples with alpha (or beta) at 1 dp, 15 with R at 3 s.f., 10 with c/R at 3 s.f., 3 with R at 4 s.f., and 33 with alpha from acos(a/R) and R at 3 s.f. verified_ok: 2022 report PDF313 (rendered): the R-form table has no SC row. PDF301's SC1 is a P1 disguised-quadratic item and PDF337's SC1 is a 2023 trapezium/log 'hence' item. The 2021 PDF236 and 2025 PDF355 general rule gives no marks when 'hence' is ignored. So D1's zero for non-hence (b) work is source-correct, and the step-3 SC1 analogy was wrong.

The 2022 P2 Q6(b) stem says 'Hence' (not 'or otherwise'). The D1 WO and exemplars keep 'Hence', and every R-form statement of non-hence credit says 0 (WO:9,72,74,82; exemplar:109; validation manual_credit_expectations).

Principal inverse: one neutral stem with a fixed tariff of 3. Bare x gives 0/3 and a bare 'no' gives 0/3. A decimal forward ratio earns M1, and the final A1 must be exact. The full inverse-substitution contradiction earns 3/3, and an unforced failed guess earns nothing. The real-solution and no-real-solution routes each have three substantive slots of equal tariff. The inverse-verification strategy works the same way for both outcomes.

Forward-only arithmetic gets the right value on 23/23 real variants but earns 2/3 (P-B1 withheld), not full marks. That is justified because the neutral stem raises non-existence, and forward-only gives only a necessary condition. It is recorded as named deviation D1-ADAPT-PI-RANGE3 from Cambridge's 2-mark item.

The conditional exact-angle link (O03:D01 for real-solution instances only) is consistent across the WO, the JSON and the coverage-plan row 73. No special-angle coverage is claimed for obstruction instances.
